title: Empty, Busy, or Both
endLine: Which enzymes an inhibitor grabs, empty, busy, or both, sets its pattern.

scenes.tts: Last time, velocity was one busy enzyme's pace times how much enzyme was busy. Now add an inhibitor. Three kinds slow this same enzyme, yet each bends its curve a different way. Why?
scenes.narration: Last time, velocity was one busy enzyme's pace times how much enzyme was busy. Now add an inhibitor. Three kinds slow this same enzyme, yet each bends its curve a different way. Why?
scenes.caption: Last time, velocity was one busy enzyme's pace times how much enzyme was busy. Now add an inhibitor. Three kinds slow this same enzyme, yet each bends its curve a different way. Why?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's world and colour map without a reset. LEFT 45% of the frame: the toll plaza, now six BLUE booths labelled 'E' (booth count schematic), YELLOW substrate cars 'S' arriving, GREEN product cars 'P' leaving, gates flipping between EMPTY and BUSY, rejected cars curving into the return loop. RIGHT 55%: the first film's computed graph, x axis '[S] (mM)' 0 to 40, y axis 'initial velocity' 0 to 60 micromoles/min, BLUE hyperbola v = 60[S]/(4 + [S]) under a BLUE dashed ceiling at 60. During the first sentence the plaza runs normally and a small booth icon rides the blue curve. On 'add an inhibitor', small MAGENTA clamp tokens labelled 'I' drift into the plaza and latch onto some booths. On 'three kinds', three MAGENTA dashed curves peel away from the blue one, each computed: '1' v = 60[S]/(12 + [S]); '2' v = 60[S]/(4 + 3[S]); '3' v = 20[S]/(4 + [S]). On 'Why?', the plaza dims back and large white text appears above the graph: 'Three inhibitors, three shapes. Why?' Keep cars and clamps moving throughout.

Title 'Empty, Busy, or Both' fades in for 2 s while the question text fades out. The three magenta dashed curves fade to faint ghosts; the BLUE curve stays. The plaza brightens again with cars flowing and gates cycling.

scenes.tts: Every enzyme is either empty or busy. A reversible inhibitor can tie up empty enzyme, busy enzyme, or both. Tied-up enzyme makes no product. Reversible means the inhibitor can come off again.
scenes.narration: Every enzyme is either empty or busy. A reversible inhibitor can tie up empty enzyme, busy enzyme, or both. Tied-up enzyme makes no product. Reversible means the inhibitor can come off again.
scenes.caption: Every enzyme is either empty or busy. A reversible inhibitor can tie up empty enzyme, busy enzyme, or both. Tied-up enzyme makes no product. Reversible means the inhibitor can come off again.
scenes.visual: The plaza grows to fill the LEFT 60% of the frame; the graph shrinks to the right. Above the booths, two bright bins sort them live: 'empty' (open gates) and 'busy' (a yellow car inside). On 'empty enzyme', a MAGENTA clamp latches onto an EMPTY booth; on 'busy enzyme', another latches onto a BUSY booth with its yellow car frozen inside; on 'or both', both happen at once. A clamped booth turns dim and sends out no green cars. On 'come off again', one clamp lifts away and that booth resumes cycling. Label 'schematic' at bottom right.

scenes.tts: First, an inhibitor that grabs only empty enzyme, usually at the active site. Substrate and inhibitor cannot bind at the same time. This is competitive inhibition.
scenes.narration: First, an inhibitor that grabs only empty enzyme, usually at the active site. Substrate and inhibitor cannot bind at the same time. This is competitive inhibition.
scenes.caption: First, an inhibitor that grabs only empty enzyme, usually at the active site. Substrate and inhibitor cannot bind at the same time. This is competitive inhibition.
scenes.visual: In the plaza, MAGENTA clamps settle only into the open doorways of EMPTY booths, blocking the slot where a yellow car would enter. A yellow car arriving at a clamped booth curves away into the return loop. BUSY booths with cars inside are never clamped: a clamp bumps one and drifts off. Large label above the plaza: 'competitive: grabs empty'. Cars keep flowing; clamps come and go.

scenes.tts: It now takes more substrate to make half the enzyme busy. At this dose, the half-speed point moves from four millimolar to twelve. That is an apparent K m. The enzyme's own K m has not changed. At very high substrate, almost no empty enzyme is left to grab. So V max stays sixty.
scenes.narration: It now takes more substrate to make half the enzyme busy. At this dose, the half-speed point moves from 4 mM to 12. That is an apparent Km. The enzyme's own Km has not changed. At very high substrate, almost no empty enzyme is left to grab. So Vmax stays 60.
scenes.caption: It now takes more substrate to make half the enzyme busy. At this dose, the half-speed point moves from 4 mM to 12. That is an apparent Km. The enzyme's own Km has not changed. At very high substrate, almost no empty enzyme is left to grab. So Vmax stays 60.
scenes.visual: The graph grows to fill the RIGHT 60%; the plaza shrinks to the left, still moving. The faint ghost '1' becomes a solid MAGENTA curve, computed v = 60[S]/(12 + [S]) (the lesson's dose with factor 1 + [I]/Ki = 3). A dashed BLUE drop line marks the original half-speed point at 4 mM (30 micromoles/min); a dashed MAGENTA drop line slides right to 12 mM at the same height, labelled 'apparent Km: 12'. On 'own Km has not changed', the BLUE 4 mM mark pulses once and stays. On 'very high substrate', a dense yellow stream fills the plaza, clamps find almost no open booths, and the magenta curve is traced out toward 40 mM, rising toward the same BLUE ceiling at 60, labelled 'Vmax unchanged'.

scenes.tts: Second, an inhibitor that grabs only busy enzyme, locking it mid-reaction as E S I. This is uncompetitive inhibition. By Le Chatelier's principle, pulling busy enzyme away draws more enzyme and substrate together.
scenes.narration: Second, an inhibitor that grabs only busy enzyme, locking it mid-reaction as ESI. This is uncompetitive inhibition. By Le Chatelier's principle, pulling busy enzyme away draws more enzyme and substrate together.
scenes.caption: Second, an inhibitor that grabs only busy enzyme, locking it mid-reaction as ESI. This is uncompetitive inhibition. By Le Chatelier's principle, pulling busy enzyme away draws more enzyme and substrate together.
scenes.visual: The competitive curve fades to a ghost; the plaza grows back to the LEFT 60%. Now MAGENTA clamps latch only onto BUSY booths, freezing the yellow car inside; the booth label changes from 'ES' to 'ESI' and its gate stops. Clamps bounce off EMPTY booths. Large label: 'uncompetitive: grabs busy'. On 'draws more enzyme and substrate together', extra yellow cars slide into the remaining empty booths as each clamp locks one, so the number of booths holding a car climbs.

scenes.tts: So half the enzyme holds substrate at a lower concentration, and the apparent K m falls. But much of that enzyme is stuck, making nothing. V max falls too. Here both fall threefold.
scenes.narration: So half the enzyme holds substrate at a lower concentration, and the apparent Km falls. But much of that enzyme is stuck, making nothing. Vmax falls too. Here both fall threefold.
scenes.caption: So half the enzyme holds substrate at a lower concentration, and the apparent Km falls. But much of that enzyme is stuck, making nothing. Vmax falls too. Here both fall threefold.
scenes.visual: The graph grows to the RIGHT 60%. Ghost '2' becomes a solid MAGENTA curve, computed v = 60[S]/(4 + 3[S]): ceiling 20, half-speed 10 at about 1.3 mM. A MAGENTA dashed drop line slides LEFT from 4 mM to 1.3 mM, labelled 'apparent Km: about 1.3'. On 'stuck, making nothing', the frozen ESI booths in the plaza pulse dim. On 'Vmax falls', a MAGENTA dashed ceiling drops from 60 to 20, labelled 'Vmax: 20'. On 'threefold', two small '÷3' tags appear, one on each drop.

scenes.tts: Here is the guiding idea. An inhibitor's pattern is set by which enzyme it ties up: empty, busy, or both. Each choice moves the half-speed point and the ceiling in its own way.
scenes.narration: Here is the guiding idea. An inhibitor's pattern is set by which enzyme it ties up: empty, busy, or both. Each choice moves the half-speed point and the ceiling in its own way.
scenes.caption: Here is the guiding idea. An inhibitor's pattern is set by which enzyme it ties up: empty, busy, or both. Each choice moves the half-speed point and the ceiling in its own way.
scenes.visual: Plaza and graph share the frame at equal size. Above the plaza, three large labelled slots appear: 'empty', 'busy', 'both'. On 'empty', the 'empty' slot lights and the competitive ghost curve brightens; on 'busy', the 'busy' slot lights and the uncompetitive curve brightens; on 'both', the third slot lights with a question mark and no curve yet. Cars, clamps and gates keep moving.

scenes.tts: Now a third inhibitor binds a separate site. It grabs empty and busy enzyme equally well. At this dose, does the half-speed point move?
scenes.narration: Now a third inhibitor binds a separate site. It grabs empty and busy enzyme equally well. At this dose, does the half-speed point move?
scenes.caption: Now a third inhibitor binds a separate site. It grabs empty and busy enzyme equally well. At this dose, does the half-speed point move?
scenes.visual: The two magenta curves fade to faint ghosts; the BLUE curve and its half-speed mark at 4 mM stay. In the plaza, MAGENTA clamps now latch onto the side of booths, away from the doorway, on EMPTY and BUSY booths alike; about two of every three booths are clamped (schematic). Label: 'grabs both equally'. Large white question card above the graph: 'Does the half-speed point move?'

Thinking pause. The question card stays. Clamped booths stay dim; unclamped booths keep cycling and sending out green cars at the slower overall rate. The BLUE curve and its 4 mM mark hold still. No other change.

scenes.tts: No. Taking the same share from empty and busy enzyme is like having less enzyme. V max falls, here from sixty to twenty. K m stays at four. This is pure noncompetitive inhibition.
scenes.narration: No. Taking the same share from empty and busy enzyme is like having less enzyme. Vmax falls, here from 60 to 20. Km stays at 4. This is pure noncompetitive inhibition.
scenes.caption: No. Taking the same share from empty and busy enzyme is like having less enzyme. Vmax falls, here from 60 to 20. Km stays at 4. This is pure noncompetitive inhibition.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves into a white 'No'. In the plaza, the clamped booths fade away, leaving two working booths that cycle exactly as before: 'less enzyme'. Ghost '3' becomes a solid MAGENTA curve, computed v = 20[S]/(4 + [S]). A MAGENTA dashed ceiling drops from 60 to 20, labelled 'Vmax: 20'. Its half-speed point (10 micromoles/min) sits directly above 4 mM, on the same vertical dashed line as the blue curve's, labelled 'Km: 4'. Label above: 'pure noncompetitive'.

scenes.tts: Pure noncompetitive is a special case of mixed inhibition. There, the inhibitor grips empty and busy enzyme with different strengths. V max still falls, but the apparent K m can rise or fall.
scenes.narration: Pure noncompetitive is a special case of mixed inhibition. There, the inhibitor grips empty and busy enzyme with different strengths. Vmax still falls, but the apparent Km can rise or fall.
scenes.caption: Pure noncompetitive is a special case of mixed inhibition. There, the inhibitor grips empty and busy enzyme with different strengths. Vmax still falls, but the apparent Km can rise or fall.
scenes.visual: Keep the noncompetitive curve. In the plaza, the side clamps on EMPTY booths grow thicker than those on BUSY booths, then the reverse, labelled 'mixed: unequal grip'. On the graph, a MAGENTA dashed half-speed mark slides a little right of 4 mM, then a little left, then settles back to 4. A small tag reads 'schematic'. The ceiling stays below 60 throughout.

scenes.tts: So before reading an inhibited curve, ask what the inhibitor grabs. Grabbing empty enzyme raises the half-speed point. Grabbing busy enzyme lowers both values together. Grabbing both equally just lowers the ceiling.
scenes.narration: So before reading an inhibited curve, ask what the inhibitor grabs. Grabbing empty enzyme raises the half-speed point. Grabbing busy enzyme lowers both values together. Grabbing both equally just lowers the ceiling.
scenes.caption: So before reading an inhibited curve, ask what the inhibitor grabs. Grabbing empty enzyme raises the half-speed point. Grabbing busy enzyme lowers both values together. Grabbing both equally just lowers the ceiling.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world: plaza left, graph right, all three computed MAGENTA curves solid beside the BLUE one. Large white question above: 'What does it grab?' On 'empty enzyme', the 'empty' slot and curve '1' pulse, its half-speed mark sliding right; on 'busy enzyme', the 'busy' slot and curve '2' pulse, both marks sliding down; on 'both equally', the 'both' slot and curve '3' pulse, its ceiling dropping. Cars keep flowing through the plaza.

End card over the dimmed but still moving plaza (yellow cars arriving, green cars leaving, magenta clamps coming and going). Large white text, centred: 'Which enzymes an inhibitor grabs, empty, busy, or both, sets its pattern.'
